 Judgment

This appeal is by the claimant in MVC.No.351/2019 on the file of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, at Raichur (for short 'Tribunal') challenging the judgment and award passed in the said case dated 27.05.2022.
02.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge, at Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The parties will be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for sake of convenience.
03. Brief facts of the case are that on 16.06.2019, the claimant was going on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 36-EP-2844 from Askihal towards Raichur on Raichur - Lingasgur road.
Around 05.30 p.m., near Bharat Petrol NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943 Bunk, he met with an accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the Trax Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-36-A-2668 by its driver.

As a result of which,
the claimant fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
He had taken treatment and spent huge amount.
With these reasons, prayed to award the compensation.
04. The respondents No.1 and 2 denied the contents of the claim petition and further stated that the respondent No.1 was holding valid and effective driving license.
The said vehicle was insured with the respondent No.3.
Therefore, the respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation.

05. The respondent No.3 denied the contents of the claim petition and further stated that its liability is restricted to terms and conditions of the policy of insurance and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

From the rival contentions of both the parties, the Tribunal had framed the necessary issues which are as under:-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner proves that accident dated 16.06.2019 was due to actionable negligence of the driver of vehicle bearing No.36/A-2668 and that he sustained injuries due to the said accident as alleged.?
II.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for award of compensation.?

If so, from whom.?
III. What order or award.?
07. The claimant has examined PW.1 and PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

The respondent No.3 examined RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.9.
08.

The Tribunal after hearing both the parties and appreciating the evidence available on record, by the impugned judgment, dismissed the claim petition holding NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943 that the claimant was minor at the time of accident and he had no driving license, therefore, he was solely responsible for the accident in question.
The same is challenged in the present appeal.
09. Heard the arguments.
10. The learned counsel for the claimant would submit that the Tribunal had not considered the evidence properly.
The claimant was not charge-sheeted for the accident.
On the contrary, the driver of the Trax Jeep was charge-sheeted for the alleged offences and he had pleaded guilty for the same.
Even the respondent No.3 had not contended before the Tribunal that the said vehicle was falsely implicated or the accident had taken place due to negligence of rider of the motorcycle.

Without there being any contentions of the parties, the Tribunal while passing the impugned judgment,
taken the points for the determination, which were not framed and given the findings.
Thereby caused prejudice to the rights of the claimant.

Had the Tribunal framed such issues, the claimant could have led his evidence in this regard and prove the issues in accordance with law.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943 11.
He further submits that the Tribunal has not answered the others issues.
Therefore, he prayed to allow the appeal and remand the matter to the Tribunal for reconsideration of the contentions of the parties.
12. The learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submits that the respondent No.3 has denied the entire case of the claimant.
Therefore, the burden lies on the claimant to prove it.
The issue No.1 is pertaining to proving the negligence.

The Tribunal on the basis of available materials on record held that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent and he was a minor; during his minority, he was riding the motorcycle on the public road, which clearly shows that he was negligent.
The Tribunal rightly considered the evidence of PW.1 and passed the impugned judgment and does not call for any interference.
13. The submission of learned counsel for the claimant is acceptable.

The issues are noted in the above paras; there is no issue regarding minority of the claimant or his is knowledge about the Mohammed Shafi @ Md. Shafi S/O Muneer ... vs Mehaboobsab S/O Dastagirisab And Ors on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106339569/
3 riding of the motorcycle or NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943 occurrence of accident by his negligence.

entities.text: Mohammed Shafi @ Md. Shafi S/O Muneer ... vs Mehaboobsab S/O Dastagirisab And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, the charge-sheet is filed against the driver of the Trax Jeep and he had pleaded guilty before the competent Court and paid the fine.
Therefore, there was no opportunity for the claimant before the Tribunal to prove his age, so also the cause of accident.
No issue was framed by the Tribunal regarding the negligence of claimant and his age for which the reasons assigned by the Tribunal.
The claim petition was dismissed on the ground that claimant was minor at the time of accident.
14. Therefore, the claimant had no opportunity to prove the facts which were considered by the Tribunal while passing impugned judgment.
Had there been pleadings and issue in this regard, then the claimant could not have raised this point.
There was no opportunity for the claimant to lead the evidence in this regard.
15. Therefore, it is a fit case to set-aside the impugned judgment and remand the matter to the Tribunal for reconsideration of the case.

16. For the above said discussion, I proceed to pass the following;
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943 ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed.

II. The impugned judgment and award passed by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Raichur in MVC.No.351/2019 dated 27.05.2022, is set-aside.

II Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: III. The matter is remanded back to the Tribunal for reconsideration of the same afresh, as observed in the judgment.
IV. Since, the claim petition is of the year 2019, both the parties are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 27.08.2024.

V. The Tribunal shall frame necessary issues of required regarding minority of claim petitioner at the time of accident and etc., Thereafter, shall give sufficient opportunity to both the side to lead evidence and decide the petition afresh.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:4943
The registry is directed to send back the Trial Court records along with copy of this judgment.
